title: VLESS-Reality: A VPN That Looks Like a Visit to a Real Website
metaTitle: VLESS-Reality Explained: The Protocol Hardest to Block
metaDescription: VLESS and Reality explained in brief: a minimal proxy protocol plus a TLS layer that borrows a real website's handshake, so there is no proxy domain to block. Speed, limits and apps.
excerpt: A minimal protocol inside a borrowed TLS 1.3 handshake from a real website. No domain of its own to block, and probes see the real site.

card.looksLike: TLS 1.3 to a real popular website

faq.question: What is the difference between VLESS and Reality?
faq.answer: VLESS is the proxy protocol: it identifies the user and says where traffic should go. Reality is the TLS layer underneath that makes the connection look like a visit to a real third-party website.

faq.question: Does VLESS-Reality need a domain?
faq.answer: No. Reality borrows the TLS handshake of an existing website, so the server needs no domain or certificate of its own. That is its main advance over Trojan and TLS-wrapped VMess.

faq.question: Is VLESS-Reality undetectable?
faq.answer: No protocol is. Research has shown TLS-inside-TLS can be fingerprinted, and some Russian ISPs were reported cutting Reality connections in November 2025. It remains the hardest mainstream option to block.

faq.question: When was Reality released?
faq.answer: Reality shipped in Xray-core 1.8.0 in March 2023. VLESS itself was proposed in July 2020.
